_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: ATO = E[e(1 - e) x effect] / E[e(1 - e)], integrated by fixture.truth_ato() and checked with scipy quad

agreement.claim: both engines report the same ATO, stacked-sandwich SE and balance
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 in every key. harness/causal_examples.test.py requires the weighted SMD to be 0 (exact balance), rebuilds the sandwich with numerical derivatives (agreeing to 1e-7), and shows the weights-as-known SE differs.

recovery.claim: the ATO is close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: The ATO and ATE differ by 0.25. At 1,500 patients and noise SD 2 the miss (0.32) exceeded that; the fixture uses 3,000 and SD 1. Measured by harness/causal_examples.test.py, running python.py on seeds 0 to 99.
